The domains flagged in the static evidence (e.g., wikipedia.org, gitlab.com) are likely references in comments or documentation within the bundled Three.js library files, which is benign.

findings.description: Static scanner flagged domains (en.wikipedia.org, gitlab.com, bugs.chromium.org, etc.) and filenames (decompress-lzf.js, three.js). These are references within the source code of the Three.js library (specifically in loader comments and documentation links) and are not active network connections or malicious payloads. The extension bundles the Three.js library locally to render 3D models, which explains the presence of these strings.

The Content Security Policy (CSP) includes 'unsafe-eval' and 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles. While common in webview-based extensions to support third-party libraries like Three.js, this weakens the sandboxing of the webview. It is not malicious in itself but is a security best-practice deviation.
